builtin.definition: Includes built-in Python types that are directly supported in PyTorch.

constant.definition: Represents constant values that do not change during execution.

ctx_manager.definition: Manages context for operations that require specific settings or states.

dicts.definition: Represents dictionary-like structures that can store key-value pairs.

distributed.definition: Represents variables related to distributed computing and parallel processing.

functions.definition: Represents user-defined or built-in functions that can be tracked and transformed.

higher_order_ops.definition: Represents operations that take other functions as arguments or return them.

iter.definition: Represents iterator types that allow for iteration over collections.

lazy.definition: Represents variables that are evaluated lazily, only when needed.

lists.definition: Represents list-like structures that can hold multiple elements.

misc.definition: Contains miscellaneous variables that do not fit into other categories.

nn_module.definition: Represents neural network modules and their components.

optimizer.definition: Represents variables related to optimization processes in training models.

script_object.definition: Represents objects that are compiled into TorchScript for execution.

sdpa.definition: Represents variables related to the Stochastic Dual Proximal Algorithm (SDPA).

tensor.definition: Represents tensor objects used in computations.

torch.definition: Represents core PyTorch functionalities and components.

torch_function.definition: Represents variables that override or extend PyTorch functionality via torch.function.

user_defined.definition: Represents user-defined types and structures that can be tracked in PyTorch.
